source.title: Cortical substrates for exploratory decisions in humans

confidence_rationale: Human fMRI: exploration is implemented as a separable MODE with its own substrate (frontopolar cortex / IPS) distinct from the value/exploitation system (striatum/vmPFC). Supports mode-as-distinct-mechanism; but the behavioural model fit was a softmax temperature (bonus-like), so it argues substrate separability more than mode>bonus.
failure_signatures: The fitted computational model was a softmax exploration parameter (random exploration), so the paper evidences a mode SUBSTRATE more than it proves a committed-mode latent outperforms a temperature/bonus.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a four-armed bandit, frontopolar cortex and intraparietal sulcus were preferentially active on exploratory choices while striatum and vmPFC tracked value-based exploitative choice -- a dedicated cortical system that switches between exploratory and exploitative behavioural modes, anatomically separate from the valuation system.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports building exploration control as a separable mode gate (a frontopolar analog) over two action-selection regimes, distinct from the critic's value estimate -- a different computational object from a novelty reward addend.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The behavioural model fit was a softmax/random-exploration parameter, not an explicit committed-mode latent; so the neural finding argues for a separable mode substrate more than it proves a mode beats a bonus at closing a competence gap.
mapping.source_context: Human fMRI, four-armed restless-bandit decision task.

confidence_components.notes: Nature fMRI; strongest evidence for anatomical separability of exploration control; caveat on the bonus-vs-mode model form. Note frontopolar locus overlaps REE SD-033e de-commit lever.
